title: Growth By Subtraction
equation: Scalable Output = Focused Effort ÷ Operational Complexity
hook: The business got bigger and somehow you got slower. That's complexity, not bad luck.
statement: Scaling means doing fewer things better, because complexity grows faster than revenue.
explainer: Every extra offer or channel adds hidden costs. More decisions, more messages, more mistakes, more switching. Cutting isn't shrinking your vision. It's protecting the work that actually pays.
sop: List every active project, offer, and channel.
Score each one's Focused Effort and Operational Complexity from 1 to 10.
Pause or drop the lowest-leverage items.
Double down on the few with the best return.
equation_example: Focused Effort 8 ÷ Operational Complexity 4 = 2.0 Scalable Output. Above 1 means you're getting more done per unit of mess, which scales. Below 1 means complexity is winning, and growth will just add chaos.
question: Name one project, offer, or channel you'll pause this month so the rest can grow.
caption:
